source_title: Business-verified January-May Passenger Vehicle Monthly Validation Workbook, May sheet
May 2026 National Passenger Vehicle Market Analysis
May 2026 National Passenger Vehicle Market Deep Analysis Report
evidence_excerpt: The business workbook reports May category sales and year-on-year changes as follows: sedans 0.6114 million units, -28.1%; SUVs 0.8228 million, -11.3%; MPVs 0.0668 million, -30.5%; cross-type passenger vehicles 0.0102 million, -30.3%.
The same workbook reports May class changes: A00 -54.9%, A0 -0.3%, A -28.0%, B -19.4% and C+ -3.7%.

The association deep-analysis page documents that its market report covers vehicle-category, country-of-origin, brand-positioning and price-positioning dimensions, and defines price bands by starting MSRP.
scope_and_caliber: May 2026 mainland-China passenger vehicles. Workbook values are the project monthly-report source of truth; the association pages are used to confirm market-analysis dimensions and vocabulary. Vehicle class and starting-MSRP price band are separate dimensions.
metric_type: Business-verified monthly passenger-vehicle validation data, with category and class cross-tabs.
comparison_period: May 2026 versus May 2025; January-May 2026 versus January-May 2025 where stated in the workbook.
contribution_or_rank_change: SUV had the smallest May category decline and the smallest January-May decline (-8.4%). A00 had the largest May class decline (-54.9%) and the largest January-May decline (-65.3%).
segment_definition: Categories are sedan, SUV, MPV and cross-type passenger vehicles. Classes are A00, A0, A, B and C+. The association defines price positioning by starting MSRP, which is not supplied by the business workbook.
structure_change: The May market is not declining uniformly: SUV is relatively resilient, while sedan, MPV and cross-type segments decline by roughly 28-31%. At class level, the main pressure is concentrated in A00 and A, whereas C+ is comparatively stable.
representative_models: Representative model evidence is provided in the separate top15_model_movements research item; this item intentionally stays at category and class level.
lifecycle_event: [uncertain] Category and class tables do not identify product launches, facelifts, production constraints or model discontinuations.
overall_judgement: May passenger-vehicle structure shows a clear resilience hierarchy: SUVs and higher classes are holding up better than sedans, MPVs and entry A00 vehicles. This is a structure fact, not yet a causal explanation; the report must connect it to verified TOP15 model movements before claiming product, policy or user-demand drivers.
observed_fact: SUV sales declined 11.3% year on year, versus -28.1% for sedans and -30.5% for MPVs. A00 declined 54.9%, while C+ declined 3.7%.
causal_mechanism: The data supports segmentation of the problem: weaker categories and classes require different explanations than resilient ones. It does not establish whether the structure came from policy, fuel costs, product launches, channel inventory or consumer preference.
confidence_level: High for category and class facts; low for causal attribution before TOP15 and external-event linkage.
alternative_explanations: A different model mix, price promotions, product cycle, regional supply, export allocation, policy eligibility and channel inventory can each affect observed category and class movements.
competitive_set: SUV versus sedan versus MPV, and A00 through C+ class groups. Price-band competition must be evaluated separately using starting MSRP and transaction price.
competitive_advantage_or_barrier: SUV and higher-class resilience is an observed market signal, not proof of a durable competitive advantage for every model or brand.
configuration_threshold: [uncertain] Class-level data does not identify charging, intelligent-driving, comfort or safety configuration thresholds.
pricing_and_profit_signal: The workbook has no MSRP, transaction-price, discount, gross-margin or dealer-profit fields. It cannot support a profitability conclusion.
target_user_segment: [uncertain] Category and class structure cannot identify household, age, city-tier or purchase-type personas.
purchase_motivation_and_pain_points: [uncertain] No user-research data is included in the category and class tables.
purchase_barrier: [uncertain] The data indicates weaker entry segments but does not identify whether affordability, financing, charging, product appeal or policy eligibility is the barrier.
channel_signal: Monthly category/class retail, orders, cancellations and inventory should be monitored together to distinguish demand from supply or channel effects.
opportunity_or_risk_grade: B signal for SUV and C+ resilience; D watch for A00 contraction. These are structural monitoring grades, not final entry decisions.
recommended_action: Require each monthly report to begin category and class pages with a single structural judgement, then use the separate TOP15 evidence pack to explain only the largest contributing movements.
regional_capacity_or_channel_action: Do not allocate regional capacity from national class data alone. Reconcile the same category and class trends with regional transaction and supply data first.
decision_condition_and_trigger: A structural signal becomes a strategic decision only when model contribution, price band, user demand and local channel evidence point in the same direction.
next_verification: Add model-level starting MSRP, realised transaction price, powertrain, region, order and inventory fields to the internal monthly dataset.
data_quality_status: Passed for category and class facts; incomplete for price bands, causal drivers, users and economics.
data_gap_or_conflict: The workbook does not label retail/wholesale scope in every cell and does not contain price or customer variables. Class must not be used as a proxy for price band.
claim_boundary: This item can state which categories and classes rose or fell. It cannot state why they changed or identify a 15-20 CNY price-band opportunity without additional evidence.
